ops.title: A daemonkit consumer migrates when it SHIPS, not when its main is bumped
ops.body:
The rule that explains why two hosts running the same fleet showed opposite migration states during the daemonkit v0.23.0 state-root move, and the reason a state wipe must be ordered after releases rather than after merges.

## The rule

daemonkit's per-daemon state root moved twice in quick succession — `~/<label>/` → `~/.daemonkit/agents/<label>/` (v0.22.0) → `~/.daemonkit/a/<label>/` (v0.23.0) — each time with **no migration and no fallback read, by decision**. A daemon creates its state under whatever root the daemonkit version *compiled into the running binary* names.

So the observable migration state of a host is a function of its **installed artifacts** (Homebrew formulae and casks), not of any repository's `main`. A consumer whose `main` carries `daemonkit v0.23.0` but which has never been tagged still ships a binary compiled against v0.21.x, and that binary keeps recreating the old directory every time it starts.

## The evidence

Measured 2026-08-29 across both fleet hosts.

`yasyf-forge-studio` reported **0** `~/com.*` dirs, **0** `~/.daemonkit/agents/*`, and **7** daemons under `~/.daemonkit/a/`. Those 7 were exactly the consumers that had *released* carrying v0.23.0 — cc-notes 0.51.2, synckit 0.38.0, captain-hook 12.22.4, cc-review 0.35.0 and their helpers. Seven consumers whose `main` was bumped but never tagged (cc-orchestrate, cc-present, reposync, cookiesync, cc-patch, binrun, cc-interact) contributed nothing to that count, because on that host they either were not installed or were installed at their pre-bump tag.

The primary workstation, same fleet, same day: **10** `~/com.*`, **4** `~/.daemonkit/agents/`, **0** `~/.daemonkit/a/`. Its installed set was simply older — cc-pool 0.66.0, cc-notes 0.51.1, synckitd 0.37.2, cc-orchestrate cask 0.16.0, cc-present cask 0.32.2.

## What follows from it

**Ordering.** Wiping a dead state generation before the owning consumer's *release* is installed is futile: the old binary recreates its directory on next launch. The wipe step belongs strictly after the upgrade step, and the upgrade step strictly after the tag. A migration plan that sequences on "every consumer's main is bumped" wipes too early and looks like a regression.

**Diagnosis.** "Is the fleet migrated?" is answered by `brew list --versions` / `brew list --cask --versions` against each consumer's released tag and that tag's daemonkit pin — never by reading `go.mod` on `main`. A repo's `main` says only that the *next* release will migrate.

**Cross-host divergence is expected, not a bug.** Two hosts on the same fleet legitimately sit in different generations for as long as their installed sets differ. Reading one host's clean state as proof the fleet is done is the error this note exists to prevent.

## Reading a host's true state

Both fleet hosts' shells differ, and this bit once: `yasyf-forge-studio`'s login shell is **fish**, where an unmatched glob is an *error* rather than an empty expansion. An unwrapped `ls -d ~/com.*` over ssh there reported a nonzero-looking result that was misread as "7 old dirs remain" when the true count was 0. Wrap every remote probe in `sh -c '...'`, and sanity-check the wrapper against a known-empty glob before trusting any count.

See also [[fleet-build-cannot-build-a-consumer-whose-module-is-not-at-its-checkout-root]] for why one consumer (cc-skills) missed both bumps entirely.
